REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - MARCH 27, 2025 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at cerritos.gov and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
Order of Agenda
The City Council, by majority of those members present, may reorder the business items listed on the agenda.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at cerritos.gov, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or in writing as described below.
In-person public comment : Public comment on business agenda items will be opened and may be provided during consideration of that business agenda item. Public comment on Consent Calendar, Closed Session, and non-agenda items will be opened and may be provided during Agenda Item No. 6.
Written public comment (hard copy or email) : Public comment may be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk at 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703 no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting and retained with the official meeting record.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 or at city_clerk@cerritos.us in advance of the meeting to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

Items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by one motion. 11A.
Report from City Manager/Executive Director
During this part of the meeting the City Manager/Executive Director or designated staff will have an opportunity to report on various City matters and/or respond verbally to questions or comments from the prior City Council meeting, including any request by the City Council to provide a brief supplemental report or brief follow-up response to items from the prior City Council meeting's agenda.
11B.
City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports
City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. In addition, verbal reports will also be provided in such cases where the City Council-appointed delegate and/or alternate is unable to attend a scheduled meeting, and there is insufficient time to schedule an agenda item for Council consideration of another alternate, necessitating a Mayor's urgency appointment. Requests may also be made of staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item, except to approve or ratify travel expenses for City-related business or to cancel or reschedule a City Council public meeting.
12.

Closed Session Report
If the City Council adjourns to Closed Session, the City Council/Successor Agency will reconvene into Open Session after its conclusion and designated City staff will provide a verbal report on any reportable action taken. This report will be memorialized in the official meeting minutes.

Adjournment

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE SUCCESSOR
AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD THURSDAY, MARCH 27, 2025,
7:00 PM, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE,
CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

  1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

  2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Bishop David Montgomery, Church of Jesus Christ Latter-Day
  Saints.

  3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Boy Scout Troup 72.

  4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jennifer Hong
  Council/Agency Member Mark E. Pulido
  Council/Agency Member Sophia M. Tse
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Lynda P. Johnson
  Mayor/Chair Frank Aurelio Yokoyama

  5.  Presentations/Appointments

  5A.  Presentations

  Proclamations were made by the City Council honoring:

  Edison Chan and Brandon Wong (Rank of Eagle Scout).

  Pinoy-Pinay Filipino Restaurant (Business Spotlight).

  5B.  Special announcement for the 2025-2026 season of performances at Cerritos Center
  for the Performing Arts.

  A verbal report on the 2025-2026 season of performances at the Cerritos Center for the
  Performing Arts was given by Jeff Thielke, Theater Executive Director. A video
  presentation was displayed.

  There was no further action on this item.

  The Mayor announced the meeting rules of decorum.

  6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period for items not listed on the meeting
  agenda but that were within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the
  Consent Calendar, and Closed Session.

  Teddy Lloyd offered congratulations to the newly elected Councilmembers and newly
  selected Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem. He also spoke in support of additional pickleball court
  placement in the City.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, March 27, 2025, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 2 of 13

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions (continued)

  Joe Pak, Senior Field Representative, Assemblymember Sharon Quirk-Silva, spoke
  regarding an upcoming event conducted in honor local women of distinction, and award
  recipients.

  Mel Cortez offered congratulations to the newly elected Councilmembers and newly
  selected Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem. He also thanked the City Council for increasing public
  comment time during this meeting, and spoke regarding public safety in his
  neighborhood.

  Deanna Allen spoke in support of the City and Los Angeles County Sheriff Department
  efforts to increase public safety in Cerritos and offered suggestions on continuing public
  safety enhancements.

  Karl Seitz spoke regarding graffiti abatement and maintenance efforts at his business
  location and submitted documents for the official record. (Documents submitted to the
  City Council at a public meeting are considered public record. Public requests for copies of
  the full-text redacted written correspondence can be made during regular business hours
  to the Office of the City Clerk).

  Celia Spitzer offered congratulations to the newly elected Councilmembers and newly
  selected Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem and requested the City Council pull Agenda Item 7C
  from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

  Pat Patnaik offered congratulations to the newly elected Councilmembers and newly
  selected Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem and suggested the City participate in the 2028
  Olympics events scheduled to take place in Los Angeles County.

  Kirit Chauhan expressed support for enhanced support for individuals who have special
  needs, at City functions. He also expressed support for the 2025-2026 season of
  performances at the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts.

  Anantha Ramachandran offered congratulations to the newly elected Councilmembers
  and newly selected Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem. He also expressed opposition to the recent
  voter adoption of Charter Amendment Measure J, which set the City’s election date in the
  City Charter.

  Elizabeth Boudreaux spoke in support of the City and Los Angeles County Sheriff
  Department efforts to increase public safety in Cerritos and offered suggestions on
  continuing public safety enhancements.

  The Mayor announced that prior to the meeting the Council/Agency members received
  full-text, unredacted copies of the one (1) written comment submitted for Item 6, by the
  deadline listed on the agenda and for inclusion in the official record. Requests for copies
  of the written comment submitted for this meeting can be made during regular business
  hours to the Office of the City Clerk.

REORDERING OF THE AGENDA
At this juncture, the City Council, by consensus, reordered the agenda to consider New and Old
Business Item 9C.2 prior to consideration of Item 9C.1.

  Prior to consideration of agenda Item 9C.1, Councilmember Tse recused herself from the
  discussion and consideration of this item, due to her ownership of property within the
  neighborhood being discussed.

9C.1. Review and consideration by the City Council of the potential closure for public safety
  purposes of one (1) entrance into the residential neighborhood bordered by 166th Street
  to the north, Studebaker Road to the west, State Route 91 to the south and Gridley Road
  to the east (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Daryl Evans, Public Safety Manager. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Mel Cortez requested the City conduct a traffic study and community survey, and offered
  additional suggestions on public safety enhancements in the subject neighborhood.

  Norma Shiota expressed support for the closure of the subject neighborhood entrance at
  166th Street.

  Yasmin Cortez expressed support for the temporary closure of the subject neighborhood
  entrance at Studebaker Road and offered additional suggestions on public safety
  enhancements in the subject neighborhood.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Johnson, and seconded by Pulido, to direct staff to:

  1. Follow guidance provided by the California Joint Powers Insurance Authority, and:
  a. Conduct a full traffic study prior to implementing any potential street closure; and
  b. Complete an extensive public outreach campaign in order to assess the level of public
  interest in a potential street closure, for the purpose of mitigating potential liability ;
